title: Weight Given to a Host's Own Declared Value on a Class Move
content:
Where a host has declared a value of their own for a vehicle offered as a Keyturn Vehicle Listing, that declared value is weighed against the adjusted figure, and how much weight it carries turns on how long the Keyturn Host Protection Plan enrolment on the vehicle has stood claim free.

1. Where the host's declared value for the vehicle sits within one tenth of the adjusted figure, that is within 10 per cent of it, and the host protection enrolment on that vehicle has stood claim free for 24 whole months or more, the declared value governs.

2. Where it sits within one tenth of the adjusted figure and that enrolment has stood claim free for fewer than 24 whole months, the mean of the declared value and the adjusted figure governs, rounded half away from zero to two decimal places.

3. Where it sits outside one tenth of the adjusted figure, the adjusted figure governs.

### Worked through on hypothetical records

Take an adjusted figure of 40000.00 USD. One tenth of it is 4000.00 USD, so a declared value between 36000.00 USD and 44000.00 USD sits within the tolerance, the boundary figures themselves being within it.

- Declared value 43000.00 USD, enrolment claim free for 30 whole months: the first clause governs and 43000.00 USD is the value that governs the listing.
- Declared value 43000.00 USD, enrolment claim free for 11 whole months: the second clause governs, and the mean of 43000.00 USD and 40000.00 USD is 41500.00 USD.
- Declared value 47000.00 USD, whatever the claim free standing: it sits outside the tolerance and the third clause governs, so 40000.00 USD is the value that governs the listing.
- Declared value 44000.00 USD, enrolment claim free for 24 whole months exactly: the tolerance is met at its boundary and the claim free test is met at its boundary, so the first clause governs and 44000.00 USD governs.
